data.title: Regulation of mTORC1 by the Rag GTPases is necessary for neonatal autophagy and survival
data.authors: Efeyan A; Zoncu R; Chang S; Gumper I; Snitkin H; Wolfson RL; Kirak O; Sabatini DD; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Rag-GTPase control of mTORC1 is essential for neonatal autophagy and survival to fasting.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway regulates organismal growth in response to many environmental cues, including nutrients and growth factors. Cell-based studies showed that mTORC1 senses amino acids through the RagA-D family of GTPases (also known as RRAGA, B, C and D), but their importance in mammalian physiology is unknown. Here we generate knock-in mice that express a constitutively active form of RagA (RagA(GTP)) from its endogenous promoter. RagA(GTP/GTP) mice develop normally, but fail to survive postnatal day 1.

extracted_findings.effect: Constitutive RagA→mTORC1 blocks fasting-induced autophagy in neonates → death on postnatal day 1 when fasted
extracted_findings.effect_size: Treatment of pups at birth with rapamycin significantly delayed the death of fasted RagA GTP/GTP neonates from ~14 h to ~21 h (p<0.01).
